question: Is the packed slot-local INT8 prefill route numerically correct for prompts that span more than one prefill chunk?
answer: No. The shared BF16 oracle pair is reused across layers while the packed executor iterates chunk-outer/layer-inner, so from the second chunk onward every layer attends over another layer's preceding K/V. Single-chunk prompts are unaffected.

mechanism.oracle_keying: hipengine/runtime/qwen35_gguf_runner.py _int8_prefill_oracle_cache_for_layer uses cache_key -1 (one shared pair) when the lifetime plan mode is layer_outer_shared_oracle, else one pair per layer
mechanism.documented_invariant: That function's own docstring: 'Chunk-outer bulk prefill revisits each layer once per prompt chunk, so it keeps one full-length pair per INT8 layer. A memory-positive layer-outer plan instead owns the full hidden plane and safely reuses one pair after each layer completes.'
mechanism.violation: _prefill_batch_native_impl chunks the prompt by _bulk_prefill_scratch.rows and _prefill_batch_native_single_slab iterates layers inside each chunk, i.e. chunk-outer/layer-inner, while the plan still selects layer_outer_shared_oracle purely from a memory comparison (use_shared = projected_delta < 0). Plan and executor disagree.
mechanism.blast_radius: The int8_direct route is forced onto this entry unconditionally by _gguf_single_row_block_table_prefill_required, so every server INT8 KV request with a prompt above the 1,024-row chunk cap is affected.

protocol.harness: scripts/gguf_prefill_route_ab.py, one process per point, fresh identical sessions per arm
protocol.prompt: deterministic varied prompt, numpy default_rng(20260909), token IDs in [1000, 32000)
protocol.kv: int8_per_token_head, FP32 per-token/head scales, max_sequence_length 16384 (no BF16 mirror, route int8_direct)
protocol.selectors: use_wmma_prefill=True, use_gemv_decode=True - matching the shipping serving owner
protocol.oracle_variant: per-layer arm forced by a local one-line patch (use_shared = False); no such env exists

evidence.note: packed rate is identical to the shared-oracle arm, so correcting the lifetime is speed-neutral at this shape; it costs memory (one oracle pair per INT8 layer instead of one shared pair)

corrections_to_prior_conclusions.gdn_attribution: The packed-vs-scalar divergence was previously attributed to 'different GDN state-capture arithmetic' on the strength of the comment at hipengine/generation/qwen35_gguf.py:7406-7408. That is wrong as an explanation of the observed divergence: with per-layer oracles the two entry points produce identical generated IDs.
corrections_to_prior_conclusions.oracle_route_speed: Earlier absolute rates from this harness (scalar 129 tok/s, packed 44 tok/s at 8,192) omitted use_wmma_prefill/use_gemv_decode, which every shipping call site sets. With them the scalar oracle route reaches 742-749 tok/s at 2,048, consistent with the retained XTX oracle-route control of 761.58 tok/s at 8,192 (results/2026-09-09-rx7900xtx-gguf-int8-direct-prefill-blocked.json). The BF16 oracle is therefore close to free, and the prior claim that a residual ~6x was the oracle's double-write/cast is withdrawn.

fix_options.a_layer_outer_executor: Make the packed path layer-outer so the shared pair's invariant holds. Preserves the memory win; largest change.
fix_options.b_per_layer_oracles_when_chunk_outer: Have the plan pick per-layer oracles whenever the executor will be chunk-outer. Correct and speed-neutral as measured, but raises the oracle cost from ~4 KiB/token to ~64 KiB/token on this geometry.
fix_options.c_rebuild_oracle_per_chunk: Repopulate the shared oracle's preceding history for the current layer from the retained INT8 store at each chunk boundary. Reintroduces a dequantized read, so it needs its own numerics gate.

not_done: No fix applied. No task-level quality measurement of the defect's impact. The 8,192-row shape and real (non-synthetic) prompts were not re-run under the corrected control.
